outlook.statement: The Company has embarked on a series of strategic and operational measures that is expected to result in the improvement in the present position. The inherent strengths of the Company, especially its reputation as a premium manufacturer and powerful brands are also expected to enable the Company to position itself during adversities. The Company has also strategically planned to address the issue of productivity and increase profits and has put in place measures to reduce cost and improve the bottom-line.

The Company has taken various initiatives to maintain its leadership, improve market share and financial performance. It has been aggressively pursuing and implementing its strategies to improve financial performance.

The Company's financial year begins on April 01 and ends on March 31. Our tentative calendar for declaration of results for the financial year 2026-27 is as given below: Quarter Ending on June 30, 2026 - On or before 14th August, 2026; September 30, 2026 - On or before 14th November, 2026; December 31, 2026 - On or before 14th February, 2027; March 31, 2027 - On or before 30th May, 2027.

Indian cane sugar market valued at USD 55.40 billion in 2025, projected to reach USD 70.13 billion by 2031 at CAGR 4.01% (2026-2031). Government support for ethanol blending, abundant sugarcane, and steady food processing demand are key growth drivers.

India expected to produce 33.6 million tonnes sugar in 2026-27, supported by favourable monsoons, improved yields, and increased cultivation area, reinforcing position as world's second-largest producer after Brazil.
Government evaluating possibility of increasing ethanol blending ratio beyond 20% through inter-ministerial committee; exploring additional applications including flex-fuel vehicles.
Industry demand for increase in Minimum Selling Price (MSP) of sugar under consideration; decision to be taken at appropriate time.
Global sugar production projected at 184.9 million tonnes in 2026/27, marginally lower than previous year; global exports forecast to decline slightly to 62.3 million tonnes.

Outlook for Sugar Season 2026–27 remains encouraging with India's sugar production projected to recover to approximately 33.6 million metric tonnes (raw value), reflecting an increase of around 12% over the revised estimate for the previous season, driven by better sugarcane yields, improved recovery, favourable weather conditions and higher cane availability in key producing States.

Domestic sugar consumption is expected to remain strong, supported by sustained economic growth, rising per capita consumption, increasing demand from the food and beverage industry and continued expansion of organised retail.

Government's continued emphasis on ethanol blending is expected to provide additional support to the industry's long-term growth by enabling sugar mills to optimise their product mix between sugar and ethanol depending upon market conditions.
Global sugar production is expected to grow from 181 Mt during the base period to 203 Mt by 2035, with 60% of the growth from Asia and 30% from Latin America.
International sugar prices are likely to remain under pressure as stock releases in India and Thailand offset shrinking production; real prices projected to ease slightly over the outlook period.

India ethanol market projected to grow at CAGR of 13.95% from USD 3.43 Billion in 2025 to USD 11.78 Billion by 2034, driven by EBP programme, E20 mandate, National Biofuel Policy, and rising sugar surplus.

With increased focus on ethanol, contribution from sugar segment will moderate in the times to come. This will help the company beat the cyclical nature of business that the sugar industry has traditionally been associated with.

The company will engage deeper with farmers, operate plants at optimal capacity and strengthen its financial performance. The company will also introduce high sugar yielding varieties released by various sugarcane breeding institutes in the country.
